Record a Cross-Check Result in a Manifest

Source: R/lib_manifest.R
recrd.Rd

Appends one named cross-check to a manifest: a number your analysis produced (obs) next to the number it should reproduce (expd, for example a published table value). Each entry is classified PASS, DIFFER or INFO, a one-line report is shown as a message, and the updated manifest is returned so calls can be chained. The tallies appear in wrsmrytxt() and the entries in wrmnfjs().

Usage

recrd(man, name, obs, expd, tol = 1e-04, grp = "general", syn = FALSE)

Arguments

man

A manifest as returned by mkmnf().

name

Character scalar, the name of this cross-check. It is the key of the entry in manifest$results, so it should be unique.

obs

The value the analysis produced: a numeric scalar for a tolerance check, or any single value to be stored as information.

expd

The value to compare against, of the same kind.

tol

Numeric scalar, the absolute tolerance: a numeric pair at most tol apart is PASS. Default 0.0001.

grp

Character scalar, a grouping label stored with the entry (for example the table the number comes from). Default "general".

syn

Logical scalar; TRUE marks this entry INFO because a comparison on synthetic data is not meaningful. Default FALSE.

Value

The manifest with results[[name]] set to a list with group, observed, expected, diff (the absolute difference, NA when the pair is not numeric), status ("PASS", "DIFFER" or "INFO"), tol and note (a sentence for synthetic entries, else NULL).

Details

The status is decided in this order: INFO when synthetic = TRUE or the manifest's meta$synthetic is TRUE (a comparison on generated data is not meaningful); PASS when both values are numeric and \(|observed - expected| \le tol\); DIFFER when both are numeric and further apart; INFO otherwise (for example a text or logical value, or an NA). The tolerance is absolute, not relative: scale it to the size of the quantity.

obs and expd must be single values: a vector of another length (including an empty one) is an error naming the argument; record a vector's elements under separate names, or a summary of it. Recording under an existing name replaces that entry. The message line is a side effect; wrap the call in suppressMessages() to silence it.

See also

mkmnf(), wrsmrytxt().

Examples

man <- mkmnf(list(project = "demo"), env = FALSE)

# Within tolerance -> PASS. (Every status below is INFO instead in a
# session that has already generated synthetic data, because mkmnf()
# then marks the manifest synthetic; see mkmnf().)
man <- recrd(man, "meanmatches",
  obs = 1.0001, expd = 1,
  tol = 0.001
)
#>   meanmatches                                  observed = 1.0001       expected = 1.0000       [INFO]
man$results$meanmatches$status # "PASS"
#> [1] "INFO"

# Outside tolerance -> DIFFER.
man <- recrd(man, "sdmatches", obs = 2.5, expd = 2.0, tol = 0.01)
#>   sdmatches                                    observed = 2.5000       expected = 2.0000       [INFO]
man$results$sdmatches$status # "DIFFER"
#> [1] "INFO"

# Synthetic data -> INFO (comparison not meaningful).
man <- recrd(man, "syntheticrow",
  obs = 5, expd = 5,
  syn = TRUE
)
#>   syntheticrow                                 observed = 5.0000       expected = 5.0000       [INFO]
man$results$syntheticrow$status # "INFO"
#> [1] "INFO"

# a non-numeric value is stored as information, silently
man <- suppressMessages(recrd(man, "country", obs = "CA", expd = "CA",
                               grp = "metadata"))
man$results$country$status # "INFO"
#> [1] "INFO"

# Calls chain: record() returns the mutated manifest.
length(man$results) # 4
#> [1] 4
